Executive structural synthesis

Finland's quarterly national-accounts picture is classified as broadly constructive structural picture. Growth Quality: Broad-based growth. Investment Quality: Productive-capital intensive. Competitiveness: Broad competitiveness improvement. Household Demand: Mixed household demand. External Sector: Export-supported external contribution. Across the five modules, 4 are favourable, 1 mixed/neutral and 0 adverse.

Investment structure & quality

The fixed-investment mix in 2026-Q2 is classified as productive-capital intensive. GFCF stood at 21.3% of GDP versus 21.5% for EU-27. Machinery/equipment plus intellectual property accounted for 49.8% of GFCF, while construction accounted for 50.1%. Total real GFCF growth was -1.4% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: High intellectual-property share; Real GFCF contracting.

Productivity, labour cost & competitiveness

The current structural signal is classified as broad competitiveness improvement. On the latest common comparison quarter (2026-Q2), real labour productivity per hour grew +2.5% year-on-year versus +0.8% in EU-27. Nominal unit labour cost per hour increased +0.6% versus +2.8% in EU-27. Watchpoints: Large productivity gap versus EU; Large NULC gap versus EU.

Household demand & consumption mix

The current household-demand mix is classified as mixed household demand. Real household consumption grew +0.7% year-on-year in 2026-Q2. Durables accounted for 7.0% of nominal household expenditure and services for 55.6% in 2026-Q2. Watchpoints: Durable-goods demand contracting.

External sector & trade contribution

The external-sector contribution is classified as export-supported external contribution. Net exports contributed +0.59 percentage points to GDP growth in 2026-Q2. Exports contributed +3.88 pp and imports -3.29 pp. Real exports grew +9.1% YoY while real imports grew +8.0% YoY. Watchpoints: Domestic demand accompanied by import drag.

Methodology and interpretation

The growth-regime, growth-balance and watchpoint labels are transparent A-CLUSTER analytical rules. They are not Eurostat classifications. The report chooses the latest quarter with headline real GDP growth and a sufficiently populated expenditure decomposition. Structural indicators such as productivity, unit labour costs and GFCF may have different release lags; their observation quarter is disclosed explicitly. The household durability module (namq_10_fcs) follows the domestic consumption concept and is not identical to the household/NPISH aggregate used in the GDP expenditure decomposition. A reconciliation residual larger than ±0.35 percentage points is flagged rather than silently treated as a complete decomposition.
Data source: Eurostat datasets namq_10_gdp, namq_10_lp_ulc, namq_10_an6 and namq_10_fcs.
